chk_problem.label: accurate
chk_problem.poster_evidence: Melody-preserving lyric editing changes the words of a singing performance while retaining its melody, timing, singer identity, and naturalness. Unlike score-conditioned synthesis, reference-conditioned editing directly accepts a singing recording and revised lyrics, avoiding costly phoneme, note, duration, and edit-boundary annotations. Removing these annotations creates a selective-preservation problem: the model must retain performance characteristics from the reference while rejecting its source lyrics.

It introduces a State-Control-Transition editing contract that separates persistent target and melody controls, recurrent phonetic-progress state, and local acoustic continuity. Progressive State-Control Grounding learns this routing without paired edit recordings.
